paragraphs.text: Judge not, that ye be not judged.
paragraphs.original: Μὴ κρίνετε, ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε·
paragraphs.translit: Mē krinete, hina mē krithēte·

paragraphs.text: For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured unto you.
paragraphs.original: ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίματι κρίνετε κριθήσεσθε, καὶ ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: en hō gar krimati krinete krithēsesthe, kai en hō metrō metreite metrēthēsetai hymin.

paragraphs.text: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother`s eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?
paragraphs.original: τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου, τὴν δὲ ἐν τῷ σῷ ὀφθαλμῷ δοκὸν οὐ κατανοεῖς;
paragraphs.translit: ti de blepeis to karphos to en tō ophthalmō tou adelphou sou, tēn de en tō sō ophthalmō dokon ou katanoeis;

paragraphs.text: Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me cast out the mote out of thine eye; and lo, the beam is in thine own eye?
paragraphs.original: ἢ πῶς ἐρεῖς τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου· Ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σου, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἡ δοκὸς ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: ē pōs ereis tō adelphō sou· Aphes ekbalō to karphos ek tou ophthalmou sou, kai idou hē dokos en tō ophthalmō sou;

paragraphs.text: Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother`s eye.
paragraphs.original: ὑποκριτά, ἔκβαλε πρῶτον ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ τὴν δοκόν, καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις ἐκβαλεῖν τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.
paragraphs.translit: hypokrita, ekbale prōton ek tou ophthalmou sou tēn dokon, kai tote diablepseis ekbalein to karphos ek tou ophthalmou tou adelphou sou.

paragraphs.text: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast your pearls before the swine, lest haply they trample them under their feet, and turn and rend you.
paragraphs.original: Μὴ δῶτε τὸ ἅγιον τοῖς κυσίν, μηδὲ βάλητε τοὺς μαργαρίτας ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων, μήποτε καταπατήσουσιν αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτῶν καὶ στραφέντες ῥήξωσιν ὑμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: Mē dōte to hagion tois kysin, mēde balēte tous margaritas hymōn emprosthen tōn choirōn, mēpote katapatēsousin autous en tois posin autōn kai straphentes rhēxōsin hymas.

paragraphs.text: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:
paragraphs.original: Αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: Aiteite, kai dothēsetai hymin· zēteite, kai heurēsete· krouete, kai anoigēsetai hymin.

paragraphs.text: for every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.
paragraphs.original: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: pas gar ho aitōn lambanei kai ho zētōn heuriskei kai tō krouonti anoigēsetai.

paragraphs.text: Or what man is there of you, who, if his son shall ask him for a loaf, will give him a stone;
paragraphs.original: ἢ τίς ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος, ὃν αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἄρτον— μὴ λίθον ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;
paragraphs.translit: ē tis estin ex hymōn anthrōpos, hon aitēsei ho hyios autou arton— mē lithon epidōsei autō;

paragraphs.text: or if he shall ask for a fish, will give him a serpent?
paragraphs.original: ἢ καὶ ἰχθὺν αἰτήσει— μὴ ὄφιν ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;
paragraphs.translit: ē kai ichthyn aitēsei— mē ophin epidōsei autō;

paragraphs.text: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father who is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?
paragraphs.original: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὄντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς δώσει ἀγαθὰ τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: ei oun hymeis ponēroi ontes oidate domata agatha didonai tois teknois hymōn, posō mallon ho patēr hymōn ho en tois ouranois dōsei agatha tois aitousin auton.

paragraphs.text: All things therefore whatsoever ye would that men should do unto you, even so do ye also unto them: for this is the law and the prophets.
paragraphs.original: Πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν θέλητε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς· οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται.
paragraphs.translit: Panta oun hosa ean thelēte hina poiōsin hymin hoi anthrōpoi, houtōs kai hymeis poieite autois· houtos gar estin ho nomos kai hoi prophētai.

paragraphs.text: Enter ye in by the narrow gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many are they that enter in thereby.
paragraphs.original: Εἰσέλθατε διὰ τῆς στενῆς πύλης· ὅτι πλατεῖα ἡ πύλη καὶ εὐρύχωρος ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ἀπώλειαν, καὶ πολλοί εἰσιν οἱ εἰσερχόμενοι διʼ αὐτῆς·
paragraphs.translit: Eiselthate dia tēs stenēs pylēs· hoti plateia hē pylē kai eurychōros hē hodos hē apagousa eis tēn apōleian, kai polloi eisin hoi eiserchomenoi diʼ autēs·

paragraphs.text: For narrow is the gate, and straitened the way, that leadeth unto life, and few are they that find it.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι στενὴ ἡ πύλη καὶ τεθλιμμένη ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ζωήν, καὶ ὀλίγοι εἰσὶν οἱ εὑρίσκοντες αὐτήν.
paragraphs.translit: hoti stenē hē pylē kai tethlimmenē hē hodos hē apagousa eis tēn zōēn, kai oligoi eisin hoi heuriskontes autēn.

paragraphs.text: Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep`s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.
paragraphs.original: Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν ψευδοπροφητῶν, οἵτινες ἔρχονται πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν ἐνδύμασι προβάτων ἔσωθεν δέ εἰσιν λύκοι ἅρπαγες.
paragraphs.translit: Prosechete apo tōn pseudoprophētōn, hoitines erchontai pros hymas en endymasi probatōn esōthen de eisin lykoi harpages.

paragraphs.text: By their fruits ye shall know them. Do [men] gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?
paragraphs.original: ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς. μήτι συλλέγουσιν ἀπὸ ἀκανθῶν σταφυλὰς ἢ ἀπὸ τριβόλων σῦκα;
paragraphs.translit: apo tōn karpōn autōn epignōsesthe autous. mēti syllegousin apo akanthōn staphylas ē apo tribolōn syka;

paragraphs.text: Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but the corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως πᾶν δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖ, τὸ δὲ σαπρὸν δένδρον καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖ·
paragraphs.translit: houtōs pan dendron agathon karpous kalous poiei, to de sapron dendron karpous ponērous poiei·

paragraphs.text: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.
paragraphs.original: οὐ δύναται δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖν, οὐδὲ δένδρον σαπρὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: ou dynatai dendron agathon karpous ponērous poiein, oude dendron sapron karpous kalous poiein.

paragraphs.text: Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.
paragraphs.original: πᾶν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.
paragraphs.translit: pan dendron mē poioun karpon kalon ekkoptetai kai eis pyr balletai.

paragraphs.text: Therefore by their fruits ye shall know them.
paragraphs.original: ἄρα γε ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: ara ge apo tōn karpōn autōn epignōsesthe autous.

paragraphs.text: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father who is in heaven.
paragraphs.original: Οὐ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι· Κύριε κύριε εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλʼ ὁ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Ou pas ho legōn moi· Kyrie kyrie eiseleusetai eis tēn basileian tōn ouranōn, allʼ ho poiōn to thelēma tou patros mou tou en tois ouranois.

paragraphs.text: Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy by thy name, and by thy name cast out demons, and by thy name do many mighty works?
paragraphs.original: πολλοὶ ἐροῦσίν μοι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ· Κύριε κύριε, οὐ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι ἐπροφητεύσαμεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δαιμόνια ἐξεβάλομεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δυνάμεις πολλὰς ἐποιήσαμεν;
paragraphs.translit: polloi erousin moi en ekeinē tē hēmera· Kyrie kyrie, ou tō sō onomati eprophēteusamen, kai tō sō onomati daimonia exebalomen, kai tō sō onomati dynameis pollas epoiēsamen;

paragraphs.text: And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τότε ὁμολογήσω αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐδέποτε ἔγνων ὑμᾶς· ἀποχωρεῖτε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν ἀνομίαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai tote homologēsō autois hoti Oudepote egnōn hymas· apochōreite apʼ emou hoi ergazomenoi tēn anomian.

paragraphs.text: Every one therefore that heareth these words of mine, and doeth them, shall be likened unto a wise man, who built his house upon the rock:
paragraphs.original: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ἀκούει μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ ποιεῖ αὐτούς, ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ φρονίμῳ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.
paragraphs.translit: Pas oun hostis akouei mou tous logous toutous kai poiei autous, homoiōthēsetai andri phronimō, hostis ōkodomēsen autou tēn oikian epi tēn petran.

paragraphs.text: and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and if fell not: for it was founded upon the rock.
paragraphs.original: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέπεσαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ οὐκ ἔπεσεν, τεθεμελίωτο γὰρ ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.
paragraphs.translit: kai katebē hē brochē kai ēlthon hoi potamoi kai epneusan hoi anemoi kai prosepesan tē oikia ekeinē, kai ouk epesen, tethemeliōto gar epi tēn petran.

paragraphs.text: And every one that heareth these words of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, who built his house upon the sand:
paragraphs.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀκούων μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ μὴ ποιῶν αὐτοὺς ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ μωρῷ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον.
paragraphs.translit: kai pas ho akouōn mou tous logous toutous kai mē poiōn autous homoiōthēsetai andri mōrō, hostis ōkodomēsen autou tēn oikian epi tēn ammon.

paragraphs.text: and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and smote upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall thereof.
paragraphs.original: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέκοψαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ ἔπεσεν, καὶ ἦν ἡ πτῶσις αὐτῆς μεγάλη.
paragraphs.translit: kai katebē hē brochē kai ēlthon hoi potamoi kai epneusan hoi anemoi kai prosekopsan tē oikia ekeinē, kai epesen, kai ēn hē ptōsis autēs megalē.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, the multitudes were astonished at his teaching:
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς λόγους τούτους, ἐξεπλήσσοντο οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Kai egeneto hote etelesen ho Iēsous tous logous toutous, exeplēssonto hoi ochloi epi tē didachē autou·

paragraphs.text: for he taught them as [one] having authority, and not as their scribes.
paragraphs.original: ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ēn gar didaskōn autous hōs exousian echōn kai ouch hōs hoi grammateis autōn.
